Coefficient Covariance and Degrees of Freedom for Anytime-Valid Inference

Source: R/inference.R
av_vcov.Rd

Computes, for an avlm object, the coefficient estimates, their covariance matrix and the two quantities the anytime-valid e-values need: the denominator degrees of freedom nu and the sample size n on which the precision g acts.

Usage

av_vcov(object, summ = NULL)

Arguments

object

An avlm object.

summ

Optionally, summary.lm(object), to avoid computing it twice.

Value

A list with elements coefficients (non-aliased estimates), vcov, nu, n, type ("classical", an HC type, or "CR1") and G (number of clusters, or NULL).

Details

  • Classical: \(s^2 (X'X)^{-1}\), \(\nu = n - k\) (Lindon et al., 2026, Section 4).

  • Heteroskedasticity-robust (HC0–HC3): the sandwich \((X'X)^{-1} X'\Omega X (X'X)^{-1}\), \(\nu = n - k\) (Lindon et al., 2026, Section 5).

  • Cluster-robust (CR1): the sandwich of the summed cluster scores scaled by \(G/(G-1)\), \(\nu = G - 1\) and sample size \(G\) (Lindon, 2026, eq. CR1).

Aliased (NA) coefficients are dropped. For weighted fits, the rows of \(X\) and the residuals are scaled by \(\sqrt{w}\) and observations with zero weight are dropped.
